findings.text: - _stat_stamps derives created/edited from st_ctime/st_mtime, but the /_discover payload the loader merges these same rows into computes them from git first/last commit time (_row_times, reckon/serve.py:1326, which prefers st_birthtime over st_ctime for created). The two payloads therefore disagree on the same document's stamps, and the section-4 merge replaces the index's values, so a row's timestamps are not stable across readiness.

- the change-watch call metadata_index.invalidate_tree(watch.root) is covered by no test: the new test calls invalidate_tree directly and no test outside tests/test_metadata_index_survives_restart.py references metadata_index, so deleting this line or passing a root that no longer matches the cache key (both sides call .resolve()) keeps the suite green while the plan's "the change watch updates the rows of the files it reports" silently stops holding.

- _covered_files re-implements the docs-tree walk (follow_symlinks=False dirs, .html selection, figure suffixes under the top-level figures dir) that discovery already implements, so the index's covered set can drift from discovery's inventory without any test binding the two together.

item_verdicts.diff: read at 2bc3b8ca. The production change is a new 333-line module (reckon/metadata_index.py) plus one endpoint (reckon/serve.py:2774) and one watch invalidation (reckon/serve.py:297); the test file adds five checks. The module reuses resources.identify_resource, _plan_html.parse_meta, file_memo.file_signature, figures._DIMS_BY_SUFFIX and write_json_atomically rather than re-implementing parsing or writing. index_rows is the only production entry point for reads and invalidate_tree the only one for the watch.
item_verdicts.done_when: the plan's done-when is met and reproduced here at 2bc3b8ca. The new test builds 140 plan files, 60 evidence files and one figure over a temporary config home; the cold build parses all 200 documents (positive control, max one parse each), and after every in-process memo is cleared the rebuild parses 0, reuses 201 rows and returns identical rows; rewriting one file makes the next build parse exactly that file and return its new title; the endpoint response carries no key outside the eleven declared fields and every declared field appears in at least one row; the negative control is executed and logged. Reproduced independently: head arm 25 passed 1 skipped EXIT=0; base arm reconstructed at 97e43902 20 passed 1 skipped EXIT=0; armed negative control 3 failed EXIT=1 including the zero-parse assertion.
item_verdicts.goal: the dispatched goal was to persist a per-project metadata index that survives a restart and answer GET /_index/<project> from stored rows and nothing derived. reckon/metadata_index.py keeps one row per covered file under <config home>/cache/metadata-index/<sha256(project, resolved docs_dir)>.json beside that file's stat identity (file_memo.file_signature), so a rebuild walks the tree, stats each file and re-parses only the ones whose identity moved; the endpoint added at reckon/serve.py:2784 serves those rows, and _FleetChangeWatch.drain drops the tree's in-process rows at reckon/serve.py:297. The plan's prose is delivered: a restart costs stats rather than reads, the row carries exactly the eleven declared fields, and the endpoint carries no derived key.
item_verdicts.manifest: its commits (1d48ac7d, 2bc3b8ca), changed_paths, tests and negative_control_log match the tree; logs/gate-head.log reads 25 passed 1 skipped EXIT=0 and logs/gate-base.log reads 20 passed 1 skipped EXIT=0, so the added-failure derivation reads a measured zero; logs/negative-control-red.log ends 1 failed EXIT=1 with the zero-parse assertion red. measurement_module and measurement_cwd are recorded for the scratch base arm. Its negative_control_note says "1 failed" where the declared seam makes three assertions red under a whole-file run; the log itself is authoritative and shows the declared assertion red, so this is a descriptive undercount only.
item_verdicts.write_paths: the section grants reckon/metadata_index.py, reckon/serve.py and tests/test_metadata_index_survives_restart.py. The two commits touch exactly those plus the evidence fragment docs/evidence/fragments/the-page-paints-from-an-index/metadata-index-survives-restart.html, which is the node's own landing anchor; the figures directory in the grant is correctly left unused. No path is outside the grant.

justifications.durability: the new checks are isolated under tmp_path with a temporary config home and clear every in-process memo, and the armed seam reddens the zero-parse assertion, so a regression that stops reusing the persisted index fails a test. Deducted because the change-watch wiring at reckon/serve.py:297 is covered by no test — the new test calls invalidate_tree directly and no test outside the new file references metadata_index, so deleting that line or breaking the root/cache-key match stays green while the plan-required change-watch behaviour stops holding — and because the index's created/edited stamps come from st_ctime/st_mtime, which move on metadata operations and differ from the discovery payload's git-derived values.
justifications.evidence: the section has both arms named as logs, the base arm run in a scratch tree with its module path and cwd recorded, and an executed negative control whose red log shows the declared zero-parse assertion failing; the cold build carries a positive control (max one parse each) so the post-restart zero is a real zero rather than an instrument that never fired. Reproduced here: head 25 passed 1 skipped EXIT=0, reconstructed base 20 passed 1 skipped EXIT=0, armed seam 3 failed EXIT=1. Deducted because the manifest's own negative_control_note reports "1 failed" where the seam reddens three assertions under a whole-file run, a description that understates what the log shows.
justifications.fit: the change is a deep, cohesive module that reuses the existing parsing, resource-identification, figure and atomic-write helpers instead of duplicating them, exports one read entry point and one invalidation, and adds a single endpoint beside the existing /_discover route. Deducted because _covered_files re-implements the docs-tree walk (symlink policy, figure suffixes, .html selection) that discovery already owns, so the two inventories can drift with nothing binding them, and because it reaches into private names across figures and _plan_html (_DIMS_BY_SUFFIX, _capture_metadata, _titleize).
justifications.goal_fidelity: every observable the section names is delivered at 2bc3b8ca: the index persists under the config home's cache dir keyed by project and resolved docs dir, a rebuild re-parses only moved identity, the endpoint serves the eleven declared fields and nothing derived, and the negative control is executed and logged. Deducted one because the plan says the change watch "updates the rows of the files it reports", whereas the change invalidates the whole tree's in-process rows and lets the next read re-stat and rebuild, so the watch itself updates nothing and the plan's wording is met only indirectly.
justifications.scope_discipline: four changed paths, all inside the grant (metadata_index.py, serve.py, the new test, the node's evidence fragment); both commits carry a conventional subject and a body with no AI trailer and no plan or sprint identifier; the two new files add no ruff finding (head 18 across the three files, all in serve.py at both base and head) and format clean; no plan state, project index or peer path is touched.
